purpose: Prove a canvas-rendered surface becomes a NAMED opaque-ledger row when it is large enough to be a real UI, is ignored when it is decorative chrome, and never suppresses capture of the readable DOM controls sharing the page. Also proves DISPLAYED_VALUES_JS grounds rendered value nodes that no interactive-control walker sees.
targeted_defect: None (regression guard). Pins the OPAQUE_JS canvas gate (40,000 px) and the separation of concerns between the three injected snippets: a canvas is not an interactive control, a premium figure is not an interactive control, and neither may be fabricated into one.

opaque.lane_note: OPAQUE_JS gates on getBoundingClientRect() area; jsdom has no layout engine so every rect is zero and no canvas would ever be detected. Asserting it in jsdom would be asserting a false negative.

describes_correct_behaviour.why: BUG-VALUE-LABEL-BLEED. This value has no label of any kind. labelOf() scans up to 3 previous siblings and 2 of the parent's previous siblings, skipping any whose text looks like a value - so it walks PAST two unrelated figures and adopts 'Surrender Charge', which belongs to $1,250.00. A value oracle grounded on that pairing asserts 'Surrender Charge == $99.99' about a page that says $1,250.00. An empty label is correct and safe; a borrowed one is a false assertion.

forbid.why: in the BODY of a collapsed <details>. The browser renders nothing there, so grounding a value oracle on it would assert against a number no user can see.
